newsitem.title: USA: Eleven die following truck collision in Michigan.
newsitem.headline: Eleven die following truck collision in Michigan.

text.p: An infant girl and a young boy were fighting for their lives Wednesday after what police called one of Michigan's worst traffic accidents in which 11 people died, including nine children.

The 8-month-old girl and 9-year-old boy were listed in critical condition with head injuries and multiple trauma at C.S. Mott Children's Hospital, part of the University of Michigan Medical Centre in Ann Arbor, police said.

Police said a dump truck towing a back-hoe slammed into a pickup truck carrying two adults and 11 children on a rural road about 6 p.m. EDT Tuesday, tearing the bed of the pickup from the vehicle's frame.
The accident occurred outside the town of Albion in south-central Michigan.
Jackson County Sheriff Henry Zavislak said at a news conference Wednesday the pickup either did not stop at a stop sign or failed to yield the right of way.

"When you look at both the numbers and the ages of the victims in this case, it's a horrific kind of accident. It's clearly the worst accident in the history of our county, and I suspect perhaps in the state of Michigan," he said.

Ten of the victims died at the scene. Three children were flown to the University of Michigan Medical Centre where one died. The dead children ranged in age from eight months to nine years. All the dead were believed to be from the Albion, Mich., area.

Police said the driver, a 24-year-old woman who also died, did not have a valid driver's license. Authorities said she was the mother of some of the victims, who appeared to be from three separate families.

Zavislak said Michigan did not have a law prohibiting children from riding in the back of a pickup. The pickup was carrying eight children in the bed covered with a camper-type top, and five passengers in the extended cab.
The driver of the dump truck was not injured. Police said he submitted to required blood and urine tests and was released. Alcohol was not believed to be a factor in the crash.

It was the second high-profile accident this summer in Michigan involving a driver without a valid license. Two members of the Detroit Red Wings hockey team were seriously injured when a limousine driven by a man with a suspended license crashed into a tree on June 13.
